subject.title: Support Azure Foundry GPT Realtime Talk via gateway relay

question: Should OpenClaw support Azure Foundry GPT Realtime Talk now as first-class OpenAI provider Gateway Relay config, and which Azure credential/endpoint contract should be accepted for the first implementation?
rationale: The remaining work crosses provider routing, new or formalized config surface, server-side credential handling, redirect safety, and external Azure availability; automation should not choose the permanent auth/security contract alone.

options.title: API-key relay first
options.body: Ship a narrow Gateway Relay path for Azure API-key deployments using the current Azure GA endpoint contract, with constrained redirect/host handling, SecretRef docs, diagnostics, tests, and live proof before considering Entra support.

options.title: Wait for Entra-first design
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers can validate Microsoft Entra or managed identity end to end, accepting a slower path for stronger production security posture.

options.title: Route out of core
options.body: Decline first-class core support and require an external plugin/provider integration, which avoids core scope but likely leaves current Talk/Gateway Relay users without the needed server-side credential path.

recommendation.title: API-key relay first
recommendation.body: Ship a narrow Gateway Relay path for Azure API-key deployments using the current Azure GA endpoint contract, with constrained redirect/host handling, SecretRef docs, diagnostics, tests, and live proof before considering Entra support.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest recent history on the OpenAI realtime provider, GA bridge, docs, and current realtime auth behavior that this decision would extend.
